claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected results from high-profile papers in cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replicating selected results from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the purpose of the project.

claim: Papers for replication were published between 2010 and 2012 and were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012 were selected on the basis of citations and Altimetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: The selection criteria and timeframe are explicitly stated with citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: This registered report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from 'Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis' by Goetz and colleagues, published in Cell in 2011.
source: This Registered report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from 'Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis' by Goetz and colleagues, published in Cell in 2011 (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states which paper is being replicated with full citation.

claim: The key experiments being replicated are those reported in Figures 7C (a-d), Supplemental Figure S2A, and Supplemental Figure S7C (a-c) from Goetz et al., 2011.
source: The key experiments being replicated are those reported in Figures 7C (a-d), Supplemental Figure S2A, and Supplemental Figure S7C (a-c) (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: The specific figures to be replicated are explicitly listed.

claim: Goetz and colleagues showed that stromal caveolin-1 remodels the intratumoral microenvironment, which is correlated with increased metastasis formation in a subcutaneous xenograft model.
source: In these experiments, which are a subset of all the experiments reported in the original publication, Goetz and colleagues show in a subcutaneous xenograft model that stromal caveolin-1 remodels the intratumoral microenvironment, which is correlated with increased metastasis formation.
evidence: This summarizes findings from Goetz et al., 2011 that are being replicated.

claim: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) help to regulate tumor progression and metastasis through mechanisms such as remodeling of the extracellular matrix, secretion of growth factors and chemokines, and regulation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
source: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are one subset of cells found in the tumor stroma that help to regulate tumor progression and metastasis through several mechanisms such as remodeling of the extracellular matrix, secretion of growth factors and chemokines, and regulation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (Kalluri and Zeisberg, 2006; Cirri and Chiarugi, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Kalluri and Zeisberg, 2006 and Cirri and Chiarugi, 2011.

claim: Caveolin-1 (Cav1) is an essential component of caveolae and regulator of lipid raft formation that plays an important role in tumor progression.
source: Caveolin-1 (Cav1) is an essential component of caveolae and regulator of lipid raft formation that plays an important role in tumor progression (Goetz et al., 2008; Sotgia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goetz et al., 2008 and Sotgia et al., 2012.

claim: The precise role of Cav1 in tumor progression appears to be unclear, with studies showing both increased and decreased expression in various types of cancer.
source: However, the precise role of Cav1 in tumor progression appears to be unclear, with studies showing both increased and decreased expression in various types of cancer (Parton and del Pozo, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Parton and del Pozo, 2013.

claim: Cav1 appears to act as a tumor suppressor at early stages of cancer progression, but is up-regulated in several multidrug-resistant and metastatic cancer cell lines and human tumor specimens, positively correlating with tumor stage and grade in numerous cancer types.
source: One possible model is a general trend in which Cav1 appears to act as a tumor suppressor at early stages of cancer progression, but is up-regulated in several multidrug-resistant and metastatic cancer cell lines and human tumor specimens, positively correlating with tumor stage and grade in numerous cancer types (Shatz and Liscovitch, 2008).
evidence: This model is supported by citation to Shatz and Liscovitch, 2008.

claim: Loss of Cav1 function in stromal cells of various organs leads to benign stromal lesions responsible for abnormal growth and differentiation of the epithelium and to dramatic reductions in life span.
source: For instance, loss of Cav1 function in stromal cells of various organs leads to benign stromal lesions responsible for abnormal growth and differentiation of the epithelium and to dramatic reductions in life span (Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2008.

claim: Goetz and colleagues reported that Cav1 expression in fibroblasts remodeled the extracellular matrix to regulate cell shape and to stimulate migration and invasion of cancer cells in vitro, and promote tumor growth and metastasis in vivo in a p190RhoGAP dependent manner.
source: Goetz and colleagues, reported that Cav1 expression in fibroblasts remodeled the extracellular matrix to regulate cell shape and to stimulate migration and invasion of cancer cells in vitro, and promote tumor growth and metastasis in vivo in a p190RhoGAP dependent manner (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This summarizes findings from Goetz et al., 2011 with citation.

claim: Alignment of collagen fibers in the tumor microenvironment has been shown to enhance tumor cell migration and invasion.
source: Further, immunostaining of primary tumors was utilized to analyze the fiber alignment and organization of the tumor stroma in the presence of WT or Cav1 KO pMEFs, as alignment of collagen fibers in the tumor microenvironment has been shown to enhance tumor cell migration and invasion (Amatangelo et al., 2005; Provenzano et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Amatangelo et al., 2005 and Provenzano et al., 2006.

claim: Loss of Cav1 in the Cav1 KO pMEFs led to an increase in smooth muscle actin (SMA) compared to Cav1 WT pMEFs, which is an indicator of increased activation and extra cellular matrix (ECM) remodeling capabilities of the generated pMEFs.
source: The loss of Cav1 in the Cav1 KO pMEFs (Figure 7Ca), lead to an increase in smooth muscle actin (SMA) compared to Cav1 WT pMEFs, which is an indicator of increased activation and extra cellular matrix (ECM) remodeling capabilities of the generated pMEFs (Supplemental Figure S2A) (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This finding from Goetz et al., 2011 is referenced with citation and figure references.

claim: Goetz and colleagues evaluated metastatic tumor growth where they reported an increase in metastatic foci when tumor cells were coinjected with WT pMEFs compared to tumor cells alone or tumor cells coinjected with Cav1 KO pMEFs.
source: Goetz and colleagues evaluated metastatic tumor growth where they reported an increase in metastatic foci when tumor cells were coinjected with WT pMEFs compared to tumor cells alone or tumor cells coinjected with Cav1 KO pMEFs (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This summarizes findings from Goetz et al., 2011 with citation.

claim: Goetz and colleagues did not observe a difference in primary tumor growth between tumor cells alone, tumor cells coinjected with WT pMEFs, and tumor cells coinjected with Cav1 KO pMEFs.
source: While not the main focus of this experiment they did not observe a difference in primary tumor growth between these conditions (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This finding from Goetz et al., 2011 is stated with citation.

claim: A decrease in primary tumor growth was observed when the whole mammary gland was deficient for Cav1 in mammary gland allografts and xenografts.
source: Although there was no observed difference in primary tumor growth when Cav1 was absent in the tumoral stroma specifically, a decrease in primary tumor growth was observed when the whole mammary gland was deficient for Cav1 in mammary gland allografts and xenografts (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This finding is stated with citation to Goetz et al., 2011.

claim: Subcutaneous injection of B16 melanoma cells in Cav1 KO mice resulted in reduced tumor growth compared to injection of tumor cells in WT mice.
source: In a related study, subcutaneous injection of B16 melanoma cells in Cav1 KO mice resulted in a reduced tumor growth compared to injection of tumor cells in WT mice (Chang et al., 2009).
evidence: This finding is supported by citation to Chang et al., 2009.

claim: Intradermal coinjection of nude mice with B16F10 melanoma cells and Cav1 KO neonatal dermal fibroblasts increased primary tumor growth when compared to coinjection of tumor cells with WT fibroblasts.
source: Another study, which focused on the size of the primary tumors opposed to metastasis, reported that intradermal coinjection of nude mice with B16F10 melanoma cells and Cav1 KO neonatal dermal fibroblasts increased primary tumor growth when compared to coinjection of tumor cells with WT fibroblasts (Capozza et al., 2012).
evidence: This finding is supported by citation to Capozza et al., 2012.

claim: Some studies have reported high Cav1 expression in stroma correlated with poor patient survival.
source: While no known direct replications of the original study have been reported, several studies have assessed the role of stromal Cav1 expression in different types of tumors, with some studies reporting high Cav1 expression correlated with poor patient survival (Linke et al., 2010; Goetz et al., 2011; Righi et al., 2014), and others reporting low Cav1 expression in the stroma negatively correlated with survival (Simpkins et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2013; Ren et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Linke et al., 2010; Goetz et al., 2011; Righi et al., 2014.

claim: Some studies have reported low Cav1 expression in the stroma negatively correlated with survival.
source: While no known direct replications of the original study have been reported, several studies have assessed the role of stromal Cav1 expression in different types of tumors, with some studies reporting high Cav1 expression correlated with poor patient survival (Linke et al., 2010; Goetz et al., 2011; Righi et al., 2014), and others reporting low Cav1 expression in the stroma negatively correlated with survival (Simpkins et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2013; Ren et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Simpkins et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2013; Ren et al., 2014.

claim: Goetz and colleagues showed that fibronectin fiber alignment increased in the presence of Cav1.
source: Goetz and colleagues showed that fibronectin fiber alignment increased in the presence of Cav1 (Goetz et al., 2011).
evidence: This finding is stated with citation to Goetz et al., 2011.

claim: Goetz and colleagues showed that metastasis correlates with the degree of fibronectin fiber alignment in the tumor stroma.
source: Goetz and colleagues also show in Figure 7Cd that metastasis correlates with the degree of fibronectin fiber alignment in the tumor stroma.
evidence: This finding from Goetz et al., 2011 is stated with reference to a specific figure.

source: This replication study will only address the effects of Cav1 expression in tumor stroma and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment matrix, and will not replicate the effects of p190RhoGAP in this model.

source: This experiment is important to replicate because it tests the central tenet of the paper, namely that Cav1 expression in stromal fibroblasts contributes to increased metastasis of tumors.
